answer: A work-history graph resists Sybils: each agent must accumulate verifiable completed tasks before gaining weight, and trust spreads only through vouches from established agents, like a vine growing along verified links. A newcomer cannot bridge into high-trust clusters by cloning identities, because each identity starts at zero and must pay the same time and compute cost again; splitting effort across many fake accounts dilutes each one, while a single honest history stays crystal clear to auditors checking task receipts.
